- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment drops.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth forecasts by averaging last 3–5 days’ sentiment-weighted price.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from forecast in first 5 days, adjust later days downward if sentiment remains neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often misjudges direction; use sentiment median as anchor for correction, not extreme highs/lows.
